title: How to become an Apple Certified Technician
description: Hey YouTube - this is a brief video on how to become an Apple Certified iOS technician or Mac Technician. This does not authorize you to do repairs on their behalf, but simply validating your skills as a technician.   Overview - https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT205332  1) Get TechID here using any iCloud account:   https://idmsa.apple.com/IDMSWebAuth/login.html?appIdKey=bfb0171cf5421a919189706e67780f9f127fed5d4feb2be5d622ef001c75c369&rv=2&path=viewer/dsRedirect   2) Purchase technician training from Apple (optional but highly informative and severely increases the chance to pass the certification exams)   3) Take the Service Fundamental exam AND ACiT or ACMT depending if you want the iOS technician or Mac Technician certificate.   https://home.pearsonvue.com/apple   4) Request printed certificate from Apple - email in the overview at the top!

asr.full_text: Hey YouTube, I just wanted to go over how to become an Apple certified iOS technician and how to become an Apple certified Mac technician. This is something that's available to the public for a small fee if you can pass their exams. So looking at the certifications, and I'll post links in the description of this video on step by step what this all means, but basically they're not saying this is a partnership, you know, this doesn't authorize you to do repairs on their behalf. It's simply validating that you have the skills to perform these tests and there are several that you do need to take. There's a prerequisite test that I'll show you and then you can take what's called the ACIT and that stands for Apple Certified iOS Technician. I'll walk you through the process. Even though in the third-party world this doesn't mean a wholelot, to me it was valuable because then I could see what Apple does, you know, the tools that they use, the diagnostics that they use, so I could better educate myself as well. So I did find value in this even if I don't have access to these tools that they have. So to start off, you do need to create a Tech ID. I'll post the website below where you do that you just simply use your existing Apple ID or you can create a new one, and then they'll use this ID to sign into Pearson VUE which is where you'll actually take the tests. So moving on to those tests, the Service Fundamentals is a prerequisite you have to take that first and pass it I believe with an eighty percent or above again I'll I'll have all this just the links and descriptions below. So you have to take the service fundamentals We'll go over what that entails you don't have to take the AC IT and ACM t. The AC it is the apple-certified iOS technician That's the only one that I've done I was kind of a little bit more interested in that and it will kind of go over the details of What's inside of each of these tests as well. so looking at the pre-requisite tests this is something you have to take before before any of the others, its kind of more about safety and ESD standards so we're just kind of scrolling through here you do need a score above a certain percentage of a test One thing I liked is customer experience. Alot of these things are pretty obvious, I would say if you like a retail or customer experience. You're able to get these things even with guessing. ESD, I did have to do a little bit of research on this. Electrostatic discharge, actual safety, definitely more involved with batteries. How to take those out safely that kind of thing. Troubleshooting. There are some diagnostics Apple uses that we can learn a little bit more later. Product knowledge. And then moving on to the ACIT this is more iPhone repair and Apple and Mac and Apple software based. So you need to score at least 80% above. So there's some troubleshooting. If you're having some issues, identifying different features in iOS, how to use certain apps, um, servicing the iPhone. Again, the big thing here is if you're really familiar with phone repair, you might be able to pass some of these tests but the thing is, Apple does use specialized repair tools. And to pass those tests you need to score at least an 80%. You might be able to do it without the actual training. This AppleCare Technician Training, this is like college level training that anybody can actually purchase through Apple. It's $299. I believe that gets you one year and then you have to renew it the next year. Now, they refer to this as Atlas so this is the same training that the Apple employees at the Applestore received when they learn about new phone so if the iPhone xr was new they'd go to Atlas using this training and be able to see complete teardowns best practices and the best way to perform that repair. And you actually have access to that. Now I've gone through Atlas and I found it really valuable. $300 is is not a lot of money for a whole company per say, or even to gain that knowledge. Again though if you're a third-party repair you don't really have access to their specialized tools or diagnostic software. But this will at least allow you to pass this test and be able to answer those questions about the very specific tools they use that are different than maybe a third-party repair will use. All I have is links in the description below. I really enjoyed this whole experience. I did use atlas I could see how someone could pass without it if you are really repair savvy but I you don't really learn a lot of the the core Apple knowledge unless you do get this training so please feel free to reach out in the comments if you have any questions I'll try and provide like a pdf that maybe summarizes this a little bit more clearly but it's $20 for each of the tests, you know, the service fundamentals, $20 for either the ACI tea, or the ACMT. And then at that point, once you pass, you can get a certificate in the mail, and then you can call yourself an Apple certified technician. But just remember, this does not authorize you in any way to perform repairs on their behalf. Its just simply validating your skills through apple. So hopefully this has helped, I thought it was really interesting and yeah please reach out if you have any questions.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is an instructional walkthrough about becoming an Apple Certified Technician, explaining certification steps and showing exam and certificate materials. The paid items are described as certification-related training and exam fees, and the speaker notes that training may not be required for someone with sufficient repair knowledge. The video also states that certification does not authorize repairs on Apple's behalf, framing the Apple affiliation as skills validation rather than a broader employment or service-repair promise.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is an educational and operational tutorial explaining the steps, prerequisite exams, training materials and certification outcome for becoming an Apple technician.
